illustrations.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a new landscape 3:2 interior illustration for Vasyl Vyhovsky's personal diary in the Ukrainian science-fiction universe Дике Поле.
Reference image 1 is STYLE ONLY: match its lightly warm off-white paper, actual graphite pencil texture, restrained dark accents, loose hatching, variable pencil pressure, faint construction lines, slight erasures, and unfinished edges fading to blank paper. Do not reproduce its park or window.
Draw the artwork itself, not a photograph of an open book or a sheet on a desk. An observant officer's personal pencil drawing, not polished digital concept art. No color, black space background, glossy shading, ink wash, watercolor, photorealism, signature, watermark or page border. Plenty of paper left visible.
Faction requirements: no national flags or paired blue/yellow bands; no modern Ukrainian coat of arms or generic three-arrow fork insignia; no decorative rushnyky, embroidered towels, sashes, waist cloth, tassels or embroidered belts. Equipment and clothing are functional. If adult male Cossacks appear they have varied moustaches and shaved-side oseledets/chub hairstyles, varied natural Ukrainian portrait-inspired faces and different poses. Kharakternyky, if present, carry only one Scythian akinakes on each wearer's anatomical RIGHT thigh, never paired Caucasian daggers.

Subject: a rough hand-drawn AFTER-ACTION TACTICAL SKETCH in an officer's diary, depicting the discovery of fifteen enemy boats and the maneuver of THREE Tavr ships around a planet. It is a schematic, NOT a cinematic space battle. Reference 2 supplies ONLY the Tavr's distinctive broad horn-shaped / crescent outline, which should be simplified into small plan-view ship symbols.
Layout and geometry: on the LEFT a loosely scribbled cloud indicates a distant radiation disturbance. In the CENTER a hand-drawn circle, about one-quarter of the page width, represents an opaque planet, crosshatched on one side. Two very faint tangent construction lines extend from the disturbance past the planet's upper and lower rims toward the RIGHT, indicating the region where the planet blocks the background interference. On the RIGHT of the planet, within that sheltered viewing region, draw a loose cluster of FIFTEEN tiny enemy boat marks. Still farther to the RIGHT draw EXACTLY THREE larger crescent/horn-shaped Tavr symbols looking back toward those enemy contacts and the planet. The enemy boats are BETWEEN the planet and the three Tavrs: the planet blocks the distant background interference but NOT their view of the nearby enemy.
Three clean curved pencil movement arrows approach from below, curve around the OUTSIDE lower limb of the planet, and terminate at the three Tavr positions on the right. Paths never pass through the planet. Avoid duplicated friendly ship silhouettes; use only the final three positions. A few restrained dashed sight lines connect them to the enemy cluster. No explosions, giant planets, detailed nebulae, decorative starfields, computer HUD, rulers, formal graph grid or infographic boxes.
Only four small handwritten Ukrainian labels, spelled exactly: "перешкода" beside the cloud, "планета" inside the circle, "ворог" near the enemy cluster and "наші" near the Tavrs. No other text. Loose personal pencil handwriting, readable but not typeset. Spare and intelligible, with imperfect circles and arrows as if reconstructed from memory.

Subject: a close observational pencil study of the heavy armor on Vyhovsky's Tavr after it survived a melta hit. Reference 2 is ONLY a construction reference for layered rectangular hull armor plates, inset fasteners, seams and nearby heavy weapon machinery. DO NOT copy its large torn breach, exposed innards, pilot, face, window, or shiny photographic rendering.
Center the drawing on a heavy irregular raised deposit of COOLED SOLIDIFIED METAL, a thick splash welded permanently ON TOP OF intact armor plating. The enemy weapon was insufficiently heated: the Tavr survived and several hundred kilograms of its metallic melta residue adhered to the hull. Show rippled metallic lobes, puckered edges, small fused beads and rough thermal scarring around a flattened raised mass. It must read as dense cold metal stuck onto the surface, NOT an open hole, crater, rock, lava or living growth. No interior machinery exposed beneath it, no deep puncture. Layered armor seams, a row of large fasteners and part of a recessed handhold establish scale. Crop a small portion of a heavy turret base in one corner only as context.
Use oblique close framing, tactile graphite hatching in the fused metal, lighter unfinished outlines of surrounding plates. No people, faces, workers, lettering, arrows, labels, steam, flames, sparks, plasma glow or active battle. Quiet aftermath: this ugly patch is a personal reminder of having survived.

Subject: an everyday transfer through a PRESSURIZED ZERO-GRAVITY passage on a warp-transfer station, seen from the narrator's viewpoint. Reference 2 supplies the approved natural Ukrainian Cossack portrait vocabulary and station-clothing style ONLY; references 3 and 4 supply hairstyles ONLY, not text or costume. Do not copy the tavern composition or its specific three faces.
THREE adult male Cossack travelers drift through a tubular utility passage with handrails on several sides. Clear weightlessness and different body orientations. Near left, a lean middle-aged moustached Cossack with shaved sides and a long oseledets pulls himself along a side rail with one hand, body at a diagonal and both bent legs floating free of all surfaces. Farther right, a younger Cossack with a forward-falling chub and shorter upturned moustache is rotated about 70 degrees relative to the first man, reaching toward a different rail; his feet are suspended, not standing. Deeper in the passage, a broad-faced older Cossack with grey drooping moustache and shaved scalp with a crown lock drifts through a circular hatch, one hand on its rim. Keep figures visually separated, anatomically credible and naturally tired or mildly annoyed rather than terrified.
All wear ordinary practical station utility jackets and trousers with compact secured equipment, no helmet needed in this pressurized passage. One small duffel bag on a short tether floats beside its owner, and one tethered equipment pouch hangs at an unusual angle. Long hair locks and straps lift subtly in zero gravity, not blowing in wind. No untethered garbage or dangerous clutter.
Strong depth through two concentric hatch frames, sparse ductwork and handrail grips; there is no single shared floor under the men. The everyday awkwardness of travel, not heroic action. Faces, hands and one rail get detailed pencil attention; far corridor trails into faint lines and paper. No combat armor, weapons, costumes, embroidery, flags, insignia, text, captions or HUD. Preserve the exact soft unfinished diary-sketch treatment.
